record.original_question: For integers n, d >= 1, let e_i(x1, ..., xn) denote the i-th elementary symmetric polynomial and let hat{e}_i = e_i(x1^d, ..., xn^d). Consider the non-standard graded Artinian complete intersection A(n, d) = K[e1, ..., en]/(hat{e}_1, ..., hat{e}_n). For which pairs (n, d) does A(n, d) have the strong Lefschetz property?

evidence.quote: Question 2.5. For which pairs (n, d) does the ring A(n, d) have the SLP?

Given integers n, d ≥ 1, let ei = ei(x1, . . . , xn) be the ith elementary symmetric polynomial in the variables x1, . . . , xn, and let ˆei = ei(x^d_1, . . . , x^d_n) be the ith elementary symmetric polynomials in the variables raised to the dth powers x^d_1, . . . , x^d_n. ... Consequently, the quotient ring A(n, d) = K[e1,...,en]/(ˆe1,...,ˆen) is a (non-standard) graded Artinian complete intersection.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $K$ be a field of characteristic zero. For integers $n, d \geq 1$, let $e_i = e_i(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ denote the $i$-th elementary symmetric polynomial in the variables $x_1, \dots, x_n$, and define $\hat e_i = e_i(x_1^d, \dots, x_n^d)$, the $i$-th elementary symmetric polynomial evaluated at the $d$-th powers of the variables. Each $\hat e_i$ is a symmetric polynomial, hence can be expressed as a polynomial in $e_1, \dots, e_n$. Consider the non-standard graded Artinian complete intersection
$$A(n,d) = K[e_1, \dots, e_n]/(\hat e_1, \dots, \hat e_n),$$
where $\deg(e_i) = i$. Recall that a graded Artinian $K$-algebra $A = \bigoplus_{i=0}^N A_i$ (with $A_N \neq 0$) is said to have the strong Lefschetz property (SLP) if there exists a linear form $\ell \in A_1$ such that for every pair $0 \leq i \leq j \leq N$ with $i + j \leq N$ (equivalently, for every $i$ and every $k \geq 0$), the multiplication map $\ell^{j-i}: A_i \to A_j$ has maximal rank, i.e., is either injective or surjective.

Determine all pairs of integers $(n, d)$ with $n, d \geq 1$ for which the algebra $A(n, d)$ has the strong Lefschetz property.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question on Lefschetz properties of Artinian graded algebras. Recent literature (2024–2025) continues to investigate the strong Lefschetz property for various families of complete intersections built from symmetric polynomials, but no complete classification of pairs $(n,d)$ for which $A(n,d)$ has the SLP appears to have been established. The problem appears to remain open in general.

status_evidence.title: A binary tree of complete intersections with the strong Lefschetz property
status_evidence.snippet: A new family of complete intersections with the strong Lefschetz property... defined by ideals generated by power sum symmetric polynomials of consecutive degrees.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work explores SLP for symmetric-function-defined complete intersections but does not resolve the classification for A(n,d).

status_evidence.title: On Strong Lefschetz Property of 0-dimensional complete intersections
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates the SLP for 0-dimensional complete intersections.
status_evidence.claim: Ongoing research into SLP for complete intersections; the specific question for A(n,d) is not classified.
